translationRepairs: Sun Quan comforted him and addressed him by his courtesy name: "Chengming, Ding Fu of old was a prisoner taken at Ruo, yet King Wu of Zhou made him a field commander;
Sun Quan comforted him and addressed him by his courtesy name: "Chengming, Guan Dingfu of old was a prisoner taken at Ruo, yet King Wu of Chu made him a field commander;

The Chinese names 观丁父 and 武王; the following units call both men Jing worthies who became famous ministers of Chu, so this King Wu is Chu’s, not Zhou’s, and the captive’s name is Guan Dingfu, not Ding Fu.

The section assistant of Wuling, Fan You, enticed the various barbarians and plotted to attach Wuling to Liu Bei; outwardly it was reported that a difference-commander should be dispatched with ten thousand men to go punish him.

The section assistant of Wuling, Fan You, enticed the various barbarians and plotted to attach Wuling to Liu Bei; outwardly it was reported that a commander should be dispatched with ten thousand men to go punish him.
差督督万人 is the verb 差 “to dispatch” plus a commander to lead ten thousand men; rendering 差 as the noun “difference” is a real mistranslation, and the replacement is accurate.
Why do you make so little of him?" Sun Quan asked."
Sun Quan asked, "Why do you make so little of him?"
权曰 opens a complete quoted question 卿何以轻之; the original English breaks the quote and leaves a stray mark after the attribution.
Gentleman attendant Xie Hong asked Lü Yi in passing how Chancellor Gu's case looked; Lü Yi replied that things did not look good."
Gentleman attendant Xie Hong asked Lü Yi in passing how Chancellor Gu's case looked; Lü Yi replied that things did not look good.
The idiomatic line is indirect speech matching 壹答：「不能佳」, so the unopened closing quotation mark is a real English error, not a Chinese quote to preserve.

If Gu Yong falls," Xie Hong went on, "who takes his place?" Lü Yi stayed silent until Xie Hong suggested, "I suppose Grand Master of Ceremonies Pan would be the one?" After a long pause Lü Yi admitted, "You are not far wrong."

"If Gu Yong falls," Xie Hong went on, "who takes his place?" Lü Yi stayed silent until Xie Hong suggested, "I suppose Grand Master of Ceremonies Pan would be the one?" After a long pause Lü Yi admitted, "You are not far wrong."
厷又問 opens a quoted question; the English starts mid-quote without an opening mark. Adding it restores grammatical quotation without changing meaning.
Lu Kai, styled Jingfeng, came from Wu in Wu commandery, a kinsman of Chancellor Sun Xun.
Lu Kai, styled Jingfeng, came from Wu in Wu commandery, a kinsman of Chancellor Lu Xun.
丞相遜 is Chancellor Lu Xun (陸遜), named by office and given name; Sun Xun invents the wrong surname from 遜.
Lu Kai, courtesy name Jingfeng, was a man of Wu in Wu commandery, a clansman of Chancellor Sun.
Lu Kai, courtesy name Jingfeng, was a man of Wu in Wu commandery, a clansman of Chancellor Xun.
遜 is Lu Xun’s given name, not the surname Sun; the literal line should read Chancellor Xun, matching 丞相遜.

When recalled from the south he marched straight to the capital, passed through Wuchang without a backward glance, and touched none of the materiel stacked there—bold in the field, restrained before gain.

When summoned to go down to the capital he went straight there, passed through Wuchang without a backward glance, and took none of the weapons and military supplies—resolute in arms, restrained before gain.
被召當下，逕還赴都 is a summons to go down to the capital and a straight journey there, not a recall from the south; 器械軍資，一無所取 and 在戎果毅 are weapons and supplies taken not at all, and resoluteness in arms.

Shu had veteran armies and rugged terrain; with gates barred it might have endured forever. Instead the Liu house grasped at power with fatal misjudgment, mishandled rewards and punishments, indulged in luxury, and squandered the people on needless projects—so Jin overran them and led ruler and ministers away in chains. The lesson is staring us in the face.

Its troops were many, picked, and strong; with gates shut and defense firm it might have been preserved for ages. Yet the Liu house, through grasping and perverse error, lost measure in rewards and punishments; the ruler gave free rein to extravagance, and the people's strength was drained on what was not urgent—so Jin attacked them and lord and ministers were taken captive. This is clear proof before our eyes.

This unit continues 益州 from the previous sentence and says 兵多精強 and 君恣意於奢侈; it does not name Shu, assign rugged terrain here, or mention chains. The replacement restores those points without adding unsupported facts.
I, Pei Songzhi, gathered from travelers out of Jing and Yang Lu Kai's twenty remonstrances to Sun Hao, yet when I asked Wu natives most said they had never seen such a memorial.
I, Pei Songzhi, gathered from travelers out of Jing and Yang, Lu Kai's twenty remonstrances to Sun Hao, yet when I asked Wu natives most said they had never seen such a memorial.
荊、揚 are the regions Jing and Yang, after which Pei obtained 凱所諫皓二十事; without a comma, Yang Lu Kai reads as a false personal name.
When wet nurses served the princes, their husbands were excused from labor, given stipends, and sent home now and then to tend their infants.

When the late emperor was alive, he too provided for the princes and the heir apparent: if wet nurses were taken, their husbands were excused from labor, given money and grain, and sent home now and then to tend their infants.
The original omits 先帝在時 and 亦養諸王太子, a real gap. The proposal restores those agents but is too literal for the idiomatic field and misreads 复役 as “again” rather than corvée exemption.

Now the overseers in each place vex the people with fussiness, and moreover there are inner agents who throw them into confusion within—one people, ten clerks—how can they bear the mandate? In the time of Emperor Jing of Han, Jiaozhi rebelled; truly it arose from this: this is following Emperor Jing's fault, not following the late emperor, seventeenth;

Now the overseers in each place vex the people with fussiness, and moreover there are inner agents who throw them into confusion within—one people, ten clerks—how can they bear the mandate? In the time of Emperor Jing, Jiaozhi rebelled; truly it arose from this: this is following Emperor Jing's fault, not following the late emperor, seventeenth;
The text has 昔景帝時，交阯反亂 with no 漢. In this Wu memorial the Jiaozhi revolt is set against 景帝 as distinct from 先帝, i.e. Wu Jingdi, so “of Han” is an interpolation.

Local inspectors harrow the people, and palace agents stir trouble within—ten clerks for every household. How can the people endure? Jiaozhi rose under Emperor Jing for just such reasons. You copy Jing's error, not your father's way—that is the seventeenth count.

Local inspectors harrow the people, and palace agents stir trouble within—ten clerks for every household. How can the people endure? Jiaozhi rose under Emperor Jing for just such reasons. You copy Jing's error, not the late emperor's way—that is the seventeenth count.
不遵先帝 is the late emperor of the memorial’s refrain, contrasted with 遵景帝之闕. Sun Hao’s father was not that 先帝, so “your father's way” is a kinship error.
Even in his father's last days, when Lü Yi and Qian Qin appeared, they were soon put to death to satisfy public outrage.
Even in the late emperor's closing years, when Lü Yi and Qian Qin appeared, they were soon put to death to satisfy public outrage.
先帝末年 names the late emperor’s closing years, when 呂壹、錢欽 were killed; calling this “his father's last days” wrongly makes Sun Quan Sun Hao’s father.
To secure the father in the capital while the heir has no foothold is the very image of sons torn from fathers and ministers torn from their lord.
To keep the father secure for long while leaving the son nothing to lean on is the very image of the son parted from the father and the minister parted from Your Majesty.
为父长安 is long security for the father, not the capital Chang’an; 使子无倚 and 臣离於陛下 are the son with nothing to lean on and the minister parted from Your Majesty.
To make the father secure in Chang'an while leaving the son nothing to lean on—this is the image of the son parted from the father, the minister parted from Your Majesty.
To make the father long secure while leaving the son nothing to lean on—this is the image of the son parted from the father, the minister parted from Your Majesty.
长安 here is the verb-object “long secure,” not the city Chang’an, which Wu’s court is not naming in this palace-building remonstrance.
Zhu could not endure the pain of poison and confessed to what he had said.
Zhu could not endure the pain of the cruel torture and confessed to what he had said.
In this prison sequence 痛毒 is cruel torment under examination, not ingested poison; the idiomatic line already has torture, and the literal replacement matches 竺不胜痛毒.
In the first year of Yongan, he was summoned to be colonel at Xiling and enfeoffed as village marquis of the capital precinct; afterward he was transferred to colonel of the left Tiger Forest.
In the first year of Yongan, he was summoned to be commander of Xiling and enfeoffed as village marquis of the capital precinct; afterward he was transferred to the left Tiger Forest command.
徵為西陵督 is appointment as Xiling commander (督), not colonel (校尉); 後轉左虎林 transfers him to the left Hulin post without naming a colonelcy.
